subject: Advance commitment billing ops roadmap and year-slice invoicing
messages:
From: Emma Jones <emma.jones@novahealth.ai>
To: rachel_kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@novahealth.ai
Date: Thu, 29 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Inquiry: advance commitment billing structure and FY split

Hi Rachel,

Thanks again for the product overview earlier this week. Our finance team is modeling an advance commitment for the next 36 months and we need to understand two operational things before we can take this to the CFO:

- Can Redwood split an upfront invoice across fiscal years (FY27, FY28) so it hits our 27/28 budgets as a billing schedule, while you still treat the payment as one upfront receipt?
- How does Redwood handle revenue recognition guidance for multi-year upfront payments (we follow ASC 606)?

I've attached our FY27 budget snapshot so you can see how the line items are organized. If you could send an example invoice layout and suggested clause language for the contract (billing/true-up/crediting), that would help speed procurement.

Appreciate a quick outline we can take to procurement.

Best,
Emma Jones
CFO, NovaHealth
emma.jones@novahealth.ai

Attachment: NovaHealth_FY27_budget.xlsx

From: rachel_kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Jones <emma.jones@novahealth.ai>
Cc: ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 29 Oct 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Inquiry: advance commitment billing structure and FY split

Emma —

Thanks for the clear asks and the budget file. Short answers up front: yes, we can issue split invoices across fiscal years to match your internal budgeting, and yes, we provide a standard accounting schedule that supports ASC 606 amortization over the service period.

What's included in the packet I can send today:
- A draft invoice sequence (one payment, invoiced as Year 1 and Year 2 slices)
- A proposed contract clause for true-ups and unused-credit handling
- An accounting schedule that maps cash receipt to monthly revenue recognition (helps your auditors)

I've attached our initial proposal PDF and will loop in Ben and Laura for the detailed journal/recognition notes. Proposed next step: a 30-minute call Monday to walk procurement and finance through the actual invoice templates and the legal clause wording. Is 10:30 PT Monday OK?

Thanks,
Rachel Kim
Enterprise Account Executive, Redwood Inference
rachel.kim@redwood.ai

Attachment: redwood_advance_commit_proposal_v1.pdf

From: ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: rachel_kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>, Emma Jones <emma.jones@novahealth.ai>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 30 Oct 2026 08:45:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Inquiry: advance commitment billing structure and FY split

Emma / Rachel —

Quick finance note from our side: we can support a split-invoice approach operationally in our billing system. Practically that looks like:

- Customer signs one SOW and pays one upfront amount.
- Redwood generates two invoice documents dated to the fiscal periods you specify (e.g., 2026-11-15 for FY27 slice, 2027-07-01 for FY28 slice). The second invoice can be marked as "deferred billing" for your internal processing.
- For accounting, Redwood records cash receipt on Day 0. Revenue is recognized monthly over the committed service period per ASC 606. We will provide a month-by-month recognition schedule (see attached spreadsheet).

A couple of practical considerations:
- Discounting tiers: If you want a stepped discount (higher discount the longer the term), we need the final term & annualized value to lock the percent by invoice.
- True-up mechanics: we typically issue credits for unused committed units during quarterly true-ups; those credits can either be applied to usage or refunded per negotiated terms.

I've attached the accounting schedule export for auditor review. Happy to walk procurement through the invoice metadata fields we populate (Invoice ID, Payment received date, Revenue start/end, Deferred revenue ledger code).

Best,
Ben Carter
Head of Finance, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai

Attachment: redwood_accounting_schedules.xlsx

From: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Jones <emma.jones@novahealth.ai>, ben.carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, rachel.kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 02 Nov 2026 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Inquiry: advance commitment billing structure and FY split

Emma —

Following Ben's notes, a few concrete items your auditors typically ask for when dealing with multi-year upfronts:

1) Paper trail of the commercial arrangement: executed SOW + invoice evidence showing the payment date and the instrument.
2) Revenue schedule: monthly recognition table that maps the upfront cash to recognized revenue by month (we can provide a CSV).
3) Deferred revenue ledger mapping: we will provide the ledger code and journal entry examples (debit cash, credit deferred revenue; monthly amortization debit deferred revenue, credit revenue).

Sample clause language we suggest for the contract (editable):
"Payment: Customer shall pay the Advance Commitment amount upon execution. Billing: For internal budget alignment, Vendor shall issue billing documents that reflect allocation of the payment across the fiscal periods specified by Customer. Recognition: Vendor will recognize revenue in accordance with ASC 606 over the service period. True-ups: Vendor will perform quarterly true-ups against actual usage and apply any credits in the subsequent billing period unless otherwise agreed."

If NovaHealth requires invoices to be dated in FY27 and FY28 explicitly to hit budget windows, provide the fiscal cut dates and we'll issue the invoice documents accordingly.

Happy to join Monday's call if you want a live walkthrough.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Director, Revenue Operations, Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.ai

From: Emma Jones <emma.jones@novahealth.ai>
To: rachel.kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@novahealth.ai, ben.carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 03 Nov 2026 16:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Inquiry: advance commitment billing structure and FY split

Thanks Rachel / Ben / Laura — this is very helpful.

We reviewed the proposal internally. Two follow-ups before we sign:

- Discount ramp: we'd like a structured annual step-down — 20% year 1, 15% year 2, 10% year 3 — applied to the annualized run-rate. Can Redwood produce an invoice schedule that shows the effective discount applied to each fiscal slice?
- True-up timing: we prefer quarterly true-ups with credits applied to the following quarter rather than carrying credits forward a year.

If you can update the proposal PDF to reflect the discount tiers and the quarterly true-up clause, and include the pair of invoice examples (one showing FY-slice dates and one showing the journal entries for recognition), we can route to legal and finance today.

If Monday at 10:30 PT still works, we'll take the 30-minute call to sign off.

Best,
Emma Jones
CFO, NovaHealth
emma.jones@novahealth.ai
